summary: Garfield County, WA L-4 tower on Diamond Peak (Umatilla NF), dated 1931 or 1937 by sources, removed about 1960; no remains described, reached by trail.

facts.design: L-4 tower with a 14 x 14 cab on a 20-foot round timber tower
facts.status_note: Removed about 1960; no lookout remains described on the summit

access.note: Mount Misery Trail from the FR-4030 trailhead; part of it not maintained; summit just inside the Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness (WillhiteWeb, undated trip report)

visit.trail_note: Under 1 mile to the summit, 500 feet of gain; trail runs just under a mile to a saddle, and trees may block the unmaintained section (WillhiteWeb)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the L-4 tower was built in 1937. FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb say 1931, and a National Archives panorama is dated August 6, 1935. The story reports the disagreement and does not pick a year.
The register and FireLookout.com give 6,397 ft; WillhiteWeb's hiking figure is 6,379 ft. The story gives the register figure and notes the other.

notes_for_editor: Brief source_pages lists https://www.firelookout.com/wa/diamondpeak.html, which describes a different Diamond Peak in Pend Oreille County (Kaniksu NF, 4659 ft, 50-foot pole tower). It was read and not used, and it should come off the brief's source list. Search hits from SummitPost and TrailChick describe that same Pend Oreille tower and were not used. The 6.1 m height rests on the 20-foot figure in the WA lookouts list and WillhiteWeb. Current access comes from an undated WillhiteWeb trip report; no closure or official status was found. No photos added.
